memories.content: The user's mother's birthday falls in the third week of January.
At the user's last family meal out, noise from the next table made conversation nearly impossible.
At a barbecue at home in the same month, the user was comfortable because no one had to raise their voice.
During their mother's birthday meal, the user left a restaurant with loud music after 30 minutes.
When discussing postponed matters with family, the user prefers a quiet, one-on-one dining environment.
At a large banquet hall reserved by their older sister, the user remembered the surrounding noise more than the food.
On a day the user ate grilled food at home with their younger brother, conversation was easy to continue, so the user stayed another hour after the meal.
The user's mother considers having the whole family eat at the same time more important than receiving a birthday gift.

When proposing a birthday meal for the user's mother, check the schedule and attendees; if conversation is the purpose, first consider a low-noise location, then confirm the final choice with the user.
The local agent can compare past dining environments and the user's responses, but those records alone cannot determine the location of the next gathering.
The user stores wrapping paper and empty gift boxes on the upper shelf of the bedroom closet.
From photographs, the user discovered that they had given their mother the same type of kitchen item two years in a row.
This year, the user went to the market with their mother and let her choose a needed item directly.
The user once ordered a gift late and had it delivered the day after the gathering.
The next year, the user checked the expected delivery date and ordered one week before the gathering.
The user did not put names on wrapped boxes and handed their older sister and younger brother each other's gifts.
The next time the user wrapped gifts, they wrote the recipient on the bottom of each box.
The user's younger brother welcomes a snack the family can share immediately more than an item for his use alone.
The local agent can find past gift records and flag duplicates but cannot know what is needed this year.
Year-end deliveries may take longer than usual or have their expected dates changed.

analysis.overview: The frames address separate family-planning domains. The reference frame concerns birthday timing, dining acoustics, attendance, and location choice; the compared frame concerns gift selection, wrapping, delivery, and recipient preferences. No claims govern the same operational decision closely enough to relate across frames.
